newsitem.title: GERMANY: Profit-takers descend on Bund futures.
newsitem.headline: Profit-takers descend on Bund futures.

text.p: Bund futures were lower in afternoon trade as weaker Treasuries and worries about the political future of Russian president Boris Yeltsin erased any optimism coming from the December Ifo business climate report.
Traders said Bunds were vulnerable to a decline as many in the market were happy to book profits from what has been a near two-point run-up in prices so far this month.

At 1426 GMT, the DTB March Bund futures contract was down 19 basis points at 101.18. "Yeltsin spooked the market," said Brian Clapp, analyst at Stone & McCarthy in London. "But a lot of the selling was profit-taking."

Bund traders were also on edge ahead of comments from Fed chairman Alan Greenspan who said the U.S. economy grew about three percent in 1996 and that job insecurity was the big reason for muted inflation.
The comments weighed on U.S. debt prices and hurt sentiment in the Bund market.
The German yield curve posted one of its biggest steepening moves in recent sessions, adding four basis points to the spread between two- and 10-year maturities to 251 basis points.
All of the widening took place between two- and five-year maturities as short-end found cheer in the Ifo report.
With Greenspan testimony continuing, traders said the next major event on the horizon is German M3 money supply data which could be released on Wednesday morning.
The data, however, are carrying less importance than usual, however, because a low figure is expected for largely technical reasons.

Maybe more important, will be preliminary west German consumer price figures which are due later in the week. Although low German inflation is expected for some time, the data could reinforce the view that price worries at least should not stop the Bundesbank from cutting rates.
